title: Theo's Wobbly Snack Tower
markdown:
Dawn broke with a brilliant burst of gold and pink. Sunshine streamed into Theo’s room, tickling his nose. “Today’s picnic day!” He bounced out of bed, heart a fast happy beat.

Downstairs, Poppy the dormouse was already nibbling a tiny seed, whiskers twitching. Ms. Vale, their kind neighbour, hummed a cheerful tune, helping prepare the picnic.

“Look, Theo, my clever chap!” She pointed to a colourful tower of snack boxes. “I’ve stacked them high for our fantastic feast!”

Theo dashed. Boxes piled, bursting with treats: big ones of crunchy crackers, medium of juicy apple slices, tiny of mini-muffins on top. He nudged the bottom box. A wobble. Gulp. The whole tower swayed, this way, that way. Thump. Snacks tumbled everywhere.

“Oh dear me!” Poppy dove behind a floral cushion.

Theo’s brow furrowed. He tried again. Big, then medium, then small. Wobble! Crash! A different order. Tilt! Splat! The snack tower would not stay up. Shoulders slumped. “Trickier than building a rocket!” he puffed.

Poppy peeked, bright eyes thoughtful. “Maybe we should look for clues outside.” She scurried under a bushy lavender plant, wonderfully sweet. A perfectly round grey pebble balanced on its side, sitting still. Next to it, a larger flatter stone. Theo joined her.

“Look, Poppy! That big flat stone is right at the bottom. A super stable base! Not wobbly at all!”

He picked up a flat stone, placed a smaller one on top. It stayed. A tiny pebble on the big stone. Perfectly balanced. He bounced on the balls of his feet.

“I get it! Balance! Biggest, heaviest things at the bottom to hold everything up. That way it doesn’t tumble!”

Back inside, a dynamic duo. Biggest heaviest box — crackers — firmly in the centre of the table. Next biggest — apples — right on top, perfectly centred. Smallest muffin boxes on the very top.

They held their breath. It… stayed. A perfect steady snack mountain. Not a single wobble.

“Hooray!” Ms. Vale clapped. “A super-stable snack tower!”

Theo beamed, chest puffing. “Heaviest at the bottom, lighter on top. They don’t tip. Steady!”

Poppy, munching a tiny muffin piece, squeaked with joy. She did not call it magic. It was a stack that had learned its manners.

Ms. Vale smiled. “Brilliant builders.”

Theo grabbed a cracker, excitement bubbling. The picnic could begin without another splat, which, for a tower, is the whole of success. Poppy claimed a muffin from the top, which did not bring the mountain down, and Ms. Vale poured lemonade beside a base that knew how to stay.
